overview:
Six days is enough to see the three faces of southern Morocco – the imperial city, the Sahara and the Atlantic – if the route is planned well. This private itinerary starts with a guided day in Marrakech, then makes a loop over the High Atlas through the valley of the kasbahs, the Dades and Todra gorges, a night in a desert camp among the Erg Chebbi dunes, and a different road back by the fossil villages of the south. It ends with a day trip to Essaouira on the ocean, so you sleep in Marrakech at the start and the end and can keep the same riad.

We want to be honest about the driving: the Sahara is a long way from Marrakech, and the loop includes three long road days (about 6–8 hours with stops). We break them up with the best sights on each road – Ait Ben Haddou, the Skoura palm grove, the hairpins of the Dades, the narrow walls of the Todra – and we use a different route on the way back so you never see the same road twice. If you prefer fewer hours in the car, the 8-day version below adds a night and a slower pace.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 6 days, 5 nights
• Start and finish: Marrakech (hotel, riad or Menara airport)
• Nights: Marrakech, Dades valley, desert camp at Merzouga, Ouarzazate, Marrakech
• Type: private tour with driver, a licensed guide in Marrakech and a local guide at Ait Ben Haddou
• Longest drives: Day 2 (about 8 hours with stops) and Day 4 (about 7–8 hours with stops)
• Activity level: easy; a 1-hour camel ride and short walks
• Meals: breakfast daily and dinner on the three nights in the south

THE ROUTE
Day 1 – Guided day in Marrakech: Koutoubia, Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs, souks, Majorelle Garden.
Day 2 – Over the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Ait Ben Haddou, Ouarzazate, Skoura and the Dades valley.
Day 3 – Todra Gorge, Erfoud fossils and a sunset camel ride to a camp in the Erg Chebbi dunes.
Day 4 – Sunrise over the dunes, then the southern road via Rissani, Alnif and N'Kob to Ouarzazate.
Day 5 – Back over the Atlas to Marrakech, with an optional second stop at Ait Ben Haddou.
Day 6 – Day trip to Essaouira on the Atlantic, with an argan oil cooperative on the way.

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
• It is a true loop: different roads out and back, so every day brings new landscapes.
• It puts the desert night in the middle, when you are already used to the pace.
• It ends gently: after the Sahara, a day by the ocean instead of another long drive.
• It is private: you choose how long to stay at each stop and can change the order of Days 1 and 6.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors who want the Sahara and the coast in a short trip, couples and friends, photographers, and families with children who are comfortable in the car.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a slower pace with an extra night, see the [8-day Morocco itinerary: Marrakech, the Sahara loop and Essaouira](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/8-day-morocco-itinerary-marrakech-the-sahara-loop-and-the-atlantic-at-essaouira/83de1c4326b29a1be3bc4936).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack layers: it can be 30°C in the afternoon and close to freezing on the Tichka pass or in the desert at night from November to March. Bring a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, a small overnight bag for the camp (your main luggage stays in the vehicle), comfortable shoes and cash in dirhams for lunches, entrance fees and tips. Majorelle Garden tickets are sold for timed slots online; we book them when you confirm.
descriptions:
What to expect: a full guided day in Marrakech – the Koutoubia, a palace, the royal tombs, the souks and the Majorelle Garden – ending on Jemaa el-Fna at dusk.

Your licensed guide meets you at your riad. You start at the Koutoubia, the 12th-century minaret that has guided travellers into Marrakech for 800 years, then walk south to the Bahia Palace, built in the late 19th century for a grand vizier, with marble courtyards, painted cedar ceilings and gardens of orange trees. Next door to the Kasbah Mosque, the Saadian Tombs hold the richly carved burial chambers of a 16th-century dynasty, sealed up for centuries and rediscovered only in 1917.

After the Mellah, the old Jewish quarter, you plunge into the souks – dyers, coppersmiths, leatherworkers, lantern makers – with a guide who knows which lanes to take and keeps shopping optional. After lunch, your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden, the cobalt-blue garden of cacti and bamboo created by Jacques Majorelle and later saved by Yves Saint Laurent. The day ends on Jemaa el-Fna as the food stalls light up.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Meet your guide; Koutoubia and Bahia Palace (about 1.5 hours).
11:00 – Saadian Tombs (about 45 min).
12:00 – Mellah and the souks (about 1.5 hours).
13:30 – Lunch in the medina (not included).
15:00 – Majorelle Garden (about 1 hour; timed ticket).
17:00 – Jemaa el-Fna at sunset; free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Majorelle uses timed tickets that sell out; we book them for you.
• The Bahia and the Saadian Tombs are busiest late morning; your guide adjusts the order to avoid the crowds.
• You walk about 6–8 km on uneven lanes: wear comfortable shoes.

INCLUDED: licensed guide and driver, riad night with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, dinner, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Fresh orange juice, msemen pancakes, and if you wish, a tangia or a bowl of harira at the food stalls in the evening.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a spectacular road day over the High Atlas – the Tichka pass, the UNESCO ksar of Ait Ben Haddou, Ouarzazate and the oases of the valley of the kasbahs – ending in the Dades valley.

You leave early and climb out of the Haouz plain into the High Atlas, through Berber villages and walnut trees to the Tizi n'Tichka pass at 2,260 m, the highest main road in Morocco. On the southern side the landscape turns dry and red. At Ait Ben Haddou, a fortified village of earthen houses stacked on a hill and listed by UNESCO in 1987, a local guide walks you up through the lanes to the old granary at the top, with views over the Ounila river. It has appeared in many films, from Lawrence of Arabia to Gladiator.

After lunch you pass Ouarzazate, the gateway to the desert, home to the Taourirt kasbah and Morocco's largest film studios. The road east follows a line of oases: Skoura, a palm grove dotted with old kasbahs such as Amridil; Kelaat M'Gouna, the valley of roses, famous for its rose water and its May festival; and finally the Dades valley, where red cliffs and rock formations rise above fields of almond and fig trees. Dinner and the night are at a hotel above the river.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:30 – Depart Marrakech.
09:00 – Coffee stop in the Atlas.
10:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass (about 15 min).
11:30 – Ait Ben Haddou with a local guide (about 1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Through Ouarzazate.
15:30 – Photo stop at the Skoura palm grove (about 20 min).
16:30 – Kelaat M'Gouna, the valley of roses.
18:00 – Arrival in the Dades valley.

GOOD TO KNOW
• This is a long day: about 330 km and 8 hours with stops.
• The Tichka road has many bends; take motion-sickness tablets if you need them.
• It is often cold and windy at the pass, even when Marrakech is warm.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• Ait Ben Haddou from across the river.
• The kasbahs of Skoura among the palms.
• The red cliffs of the Dades at sunset.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the narrow walls of the Todra Gorge in the morning, the fossils of Erfoud in the afternoon, and a camel ride at sunset into the dunes of the Erg Chebbi for a night in a desert camp.

In the morning you can drive a little way up the Dades gorge to the famous hairpin bends before heading east to Tinghir, a long palm oasis below the mountains. Just beyond, the Todra Gorge narrows to about 10 metres between limestone walls up to 300 m high, with a clear stream running at their foot. You walk through the narrowest part, where climbers often hang on the rock faces.

The road then crosses the open desert plains past Tinejdad and its khettaras, the old underground water channels, to Erfoud, where a workshop shows you how black limestone full of 350-million-year-old fossils is cut and polished. In the late afternoon you reach Merzouga at the foot of the Erg Chebbi, where the dunes rise up to about 150 m. You leave your main luggage in the vehicle and ride a camel into the sand as the dunes turn orange and red. At the camp, dinner is served in a tent, followed by drums around the fire and a sky full of stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart the Dades valley.
09:30 – Tinghir and the palm grove.
10:00 – Walk in the Todra Gorge (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Fossil workshop in Erfoud (about 30 min).
16:30 – Arrival in Merzouga.
17:00 – Camel ride into the dunes at sunset (about 1–1.5 hours).
19:00 – Desert camp: dinner, music and stars.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring a small bag for the night; the camp has blankets and toilets.
• Desert nights are cold from November to March; wear layers.
• Buying fossils is optional.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, camel trek, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The narrowest part of the Todra Gorge in morning light.
• Camel shadows on the dunes at sunset.
• The Milky Way above the camp on clear nights.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: sunrise over the dunes, then a long, beautiful road across the south – Rissani, the fossil villages and the kasbahs of N'Kob – to Ouarzazate.

Wake before dawn and climb a dune to watch the sun rise over the Sahara. After breakfast at the camp you ride or walk back to Merzouga, shower at a partner hotel and set off west. You pass Rissani, the historic heart of the Tafilalet and near the ruins of Sijilmassa, the great medieval caravan city.

Instead of returning by the same road, you take the southern route between the Jebel Saghro mountains and the desert. Alnif is known for its trilobite fossils; Tazzarine for its acacias and nomad camps; and N'Kob for its dozens of earthen kasbahs, some now restored as guesthouses. The road then follows the Draa valley to Agdz and climbs over a pass to Ouarzazate, where you spend the night.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise over the dunes.
07:00 – Breakfast at the camp, return to Merzouga.
08:30 – Depart Merzouga.
09:15 – Rissani.
11:00 – Alnif and its fossils (about 20 min).
13:00 – N'Kob, village of kasbahs; lunch (not included).
15:30 – Agdz and the Draa valley.
17:00 – Arrival in Ouarzazate.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Another long day: about 370 km and 7–8 hours with stops.
• Rissani has a big market on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays.
• If you arrive in time, visit the Taourirt kasbah in Ouarzazate.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Ouarzazate.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: a shorter drive back over the High Atlas to Marrakech, with an optional second visit to Ait Ben Haddou in the soft morning light.

After breakfast you can return to Ait Ben Haddou if you would like to cross the river and climb to the granary on your own, or see the Atlas Film Studios in Ouarzazate. Then the road climbs again to the Tizi n'Tichka and winds down through the villages of the northern slopes, with a stop at a women's argan cooperative or a viewpoint if you wish. You arrive in Marrakech in the mid-afternoon with time to rest at your riad or go back to the souks.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart Ouarzazate.
09:30 – Ait Ben Haddou (optional, about 1 hour).
12:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass.
13:00 – Lunch in the Atlas (not included).
15:00 – Arrival in Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 200 km and 4–5 hours with stops.
• Your afternoon and evening in Marrakech are free.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a relaxed day on the Atlantic – the argan country, Essaouira's ramparts, fishing port and medina – and back to Marrakech in the evening.

You drive west across the plains and into the argan forest, which grows naturally only in this corner of Morocco. At a women's cooperative you see how the nuts are cracked by hand and pressed into oil, and taste amlou with bread. You may see goats in the argan trees on the way.

Essaouira is a white and blue town behind 18th-century sea walls, designed for Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah and listed by UNESCO in 2001. Walk the Skala de la Ville ramparts with their old cannons, watch the blue boats unload at the fishing port, eat grilled fish at the port stalls, and wander through the medina's galleries and thuya-wood workshops. In the late afternoon your driver takes you back to Marrakech, where the tour ends.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Depart Marrakech.
10:30 – Argan oil cooperative (about 30 min).
11:30 – Arrival in Essaouira; free time in the port, ramparts and medina (about 5 hours).
13:00 – Grilled fish at the port (not included).
16:30 – Depart Essaouira.
19:00 – Arrival in Marrakech; end of the tour.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Essaouira is windy most of the year; bring a light jacket.
• If you prefer, you can stay the night in Essaouira and end the tour there, or continue to Casablanca.
• If your flight is on Day 6, we can swap this day with Day 1 or drop you at the airport instead.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, bottled water, drop-off in Marrakech.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: Marrakech, the Atlas, the Sahara and the ocean in six days, with a different road every day.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guides are only for your group, so you can change the pace, linger at a stop or skip one.

faq.question: How many nights are in the desert?
faq.answer: One night in a camp among the Erg Chebbi dunes at Merzouga, on Day 3, with a camel ride at sunset and sunrise the next morning.

faq.question: How much driving is there?
faq.answer: Days 2 and 4 are long (about 8 hours including stops), Day 3 about 5 hours, Day 5 about 4–5 hours, and Day 6 about 5 hours return. Day 1 has almost no driving.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast every day and dinner on the three nights in the south (Dades, desert camp and Ouarzazate). Lunches and dinners in Marrakech are not included.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: A camp of Berber-style tents in the dunes, with beds, blankets and toilets. Standard camps have shared facilities; luxury camps have private tents with en-suite bathrooms, depending on the package you choose.

faq.question: Can I do the camel ride if I have never ridden?
faq.answer: Yes. The camels walk slowly and each one is led by a cameleer. The ride takes about 1–1.5 hours each way. If you prefer, you can walk or reach the camp by 4x4.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: Layers (warm for nights and the pass, light for the day), a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, comfortable shoes, sunscreen, a small bag for the desert night and some cash in dirhams.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who are comfortable with long drives. They usually love the camels and the dunes. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November are ideal. Summer is very hot in the desert, and winter nights are cold, but the trip runs all year.

faq.question: Can the order of the days be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. You can start with Essaouira or end with the guided Marrakech day, and we can move the Essaouira day before the desert if it suits your flights.

faq.question: Can I add more time?
faq.answer: Yes. We recommend the 8-day version if you want a slower pace, or you can add a second desert night, a night in Essaouira or a day in the Atlas.

faq.question: Do we need to book Majorelle Garden in advance?
faq.answer: Yes. Tickets are sold online for a specific time and often sell out. We book them for you for Day 1.

faq.question: Can the tour start at Marrakech airport?
faq.answer: Yes. We can pick you up at Menara airport on arrival and take you to your riad, and drop you there at the end.
